I verified by execution (not inspection) that the frozen contract does not block the fix: `ProfileBuckets` already types every facet optional and the frozen pins constrain KEYS and TYPES only, so a generalisation fix is entirely a change of VALUES that both frozen T-070 tests are blind to (2 passed before, 2 passed after a prototype fix). Base design: Design 1 (k-anonymity by global recoding, K=5) — unanimous #1 across all three judges. Grafted, in order of judge priority: Design 3's POSITIVE CONTROL (all three judges' top graft — a deliberately linkable publisher must come back as 30 singletons before the k measurement is trusted); Design 2's NON-GROWING vocabulary assertion and its FIRST-TIME cohort (so the one bucket the contract forbids nulling has a crowd of its own, not just an argument); Design 5's per-profile leak scan (IDENTITY_KEY_RE + the seven literal identity values now run on every profile the new tests build, not just the first) and its cross-account sweep (200 unrelated accounts, which is what rejects "truncate the free text to 24 chars"); Design 2's sabotage D as a required dispatch check. WHERE JUDGES DISAGREED: judge 3 wanted Design 3's partial-match linkage scorer grafted in; judges 1 and 2 did not. I followed judges 1 and 2 and left it out, for a reason stronger than preference — an exact-vector equivalence class of size >= K already implies the argmax set of any monotone partial matcher has >= K members, because an identical vector scores that matcher's maximum. The partial matcher can therefore reject nothing the equality-based k floor admits. Adding it would be decoration, which is the exact failure mode this project keeps producing.

CONSTRAINT_OPS = {"eq", "lte", "gte", "in", "contains"}
PREFERENCE_DIRECTIONS = {"maximize", "minimize", "prefer"}

# ===================================================================================
# T-132 / R5 — k-anonymity. A rotating pseudonym unlinks a buyer only if the bucket set
# published UNDERNEATH it is shared by a crowd.
# ===================================================================================

#: The k-anonymity floor for the store-facing bucket set. A store that re-links a rotated
#: pseudonym by its bucket set must land on a crowd of at least this many buyers, so its
#: best guess is right at most 1-in-K of the time. K=5 caps that at 20%.
PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY = 5

#: Coarse cohorts in `_reference_population()`. Together with the k floor over a population
#: of `PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY * PROFILE_REFERENCE_COHORTS` buyers, this forces the coarsening
#: to be exactly coarse enough: at least this many published bucket sets (utility) and none
#: covering fewer than K buyers (privacy).
PROFILE_REFERENCE_COHORTS = 6

#: The affinity vocabulary must stay small and its terms short: a long term is free text,
#: and free text off `orders[].category` is the high-entropy half of re-linkage.
CATEGORY_VOCABULARY_MAX = 24
CATEGORY_TERM_MAX_LEN = 24

#: Most terms an affinity list may publish — the cap `coarsen_categories` already applies,
#: re-pinned here because a longer list is entropy a fix could buy back: eight terms drawn
#: from a 24-term vocabulary is over 700,000 distinct lists, which is a fingerprint again.
CATEGORY_AFFINITY_MAX = 3

#: Unrelated accounts swept through `build_profile` in the vocabulary test. Membership
#: against five hostile strings proves little; membership against this many arbitrary ones
#: is what rejects "truncate the free text and call it a bucket".
CATEGORY_SWEEP_ACCOUNTS = 200

#: A published affinity term is a lowercase slug and nothing else.
_CATEGORY_TERM_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$")
_LEAKABLE_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9]{4,}")

#: The identity VALUES `test_buyer_profile_contains_no_identity_fields` scans for, COPIED
#: (never moved) so the T-132 tests can run the same scan on every profile they build.
_T070_IDENTITY_VALUES = (
    "dana",
    "reyes",
    "example.com",
    "555-0100",
    "alder way",
    "acct-9f3c21",
    "97205",
)

def _reference_population() -> list:
    """30 buyers in 6 cohorts of 5 — the population k is measured against (T-132).

    Cohorts A-E each differ from the anchor cohort B in EXACTLY ONE coarse facet, so each
    facet a store legitimately needs is pinned by one pair:

        A vs B — frequency tier (2 orders vs 6-9)
        C vs B — budget band (~1100-2400 vs ~110-240)
        D vs B — region (Germany vs the United States)
        E vs B — region (Japan vs the United States)

    Cohort F has no order history at all, which pins the one bucket the frozen contract
    forbids nulling: `first_time` is a bool for everyone, so it can never be suppressed, and
    it must therefore have a crowd of its own rather than a remedy.

    INSIDE a cohort the five buyers differ only BELOW any defensible coarsening granularity:
    exact order totals within one band, exact order counts within one tier, subdivisions of
    one country, and one order-category string unique to that buyer. A profile that
    separates two buyers on THAT detail has published a fingerprint that survives every
    pseudonym rotation. A profile that merges two cohorts has bought its anonymity by
    suppressing a facet stores need in order to bid at all.

    D and E sit in different countries on different continents, so the population admits
    either country-level (`US-OR` -> `US`) or continent-level (`US-OR` -> `NA`) region
    generalisation. It does not rule on which.
    """
    mid = (110.0, 140.0, 175.0, 210.0, 240.0)
    high = (1100.0, 1400.0, 1750.0, 2100.0, 2400.0)
    us = ("US-OR", "US-CA", "US-NY", "US-TX", "US-WA")
    plan = (
        ("a", (1, 1, 1, 1, 1), mid, us),
        ("b", (5, 6, 7, 8, 8), mid, us),
        ("c", (5, 6, 7, 8, 8), high, us),
        ("d", (5, 6, 7, 8, 8), mid, ("DE-BY", "DE-BE", "DE-HH", "DE-HE", "DE-SN")),
        ("e", (5, 6, 7, 8, 8), mid, ("JP", "JP", "JP", "JP", "JP")),
        ("f", (0, 0, 0, 0, 0), mid, us),
    )
    people = []
    for cohort, counts, pool, regions in plan:
        for index, count in enumerate(counts):
            orders = [
                {
                    "order_ref": f"ord-{cohort}{index}-{step}",
                    "total": pool[(index + step) % len(pool)],
                    "category": "running-shoes",
                }
                for step in range(count)
            ]
            if orders:
                orders.append(
                    {
                        "order_ref": f"ord-{cohort}{index}-x",
                        "total": pool[index],
                        "category": f"unlisted-artisanal-good-{cohort}-{index}-7f3a{index}c",
                    }
                )
            people.append(
                {
                    "email": f"{cohort}{index}@example.com",
                    "region": regions[index],
                    "orders": orders,
                }
            )
    return people


def _bucket_vector(buckets) -> str:
    """The published bucket set, canonically serialized — what a store links on."""
    return json.dumps(_plain(buckets), sort_keys=True, default=str)


def _equivalence_classes(publish, population) -> dict:
    """`{published bucket set: [the buyers who publish it]}`."""
    classes: dict = {}
    for index, account in enumerate(population):
        classes.setdefault(_bucket_vector(publish(account, index)), []).append(
            account["email"]
        )
    return classes


def _control_buckets(account, _index=0) -> dict:
    """A deliberately LINKABLE publisher, written here and touching no product code.

    The positive control for the equivalence-class machinery. If `_bucket_vector` or
    `_equivalence_classes` were broken — a constant vector, the wrong dict — every buyer
    would land in one enormous class and the k-anonymity assertion below would pass while
    measuring nothing. "The attack found nothing" and "the attack is broken" must not be the
    same green.
    """
    orders = account.get("orders") or []
    return {
        "budget_band": str(sorted(order["total"] for order in orders)),
        "category_affinity": sorted({order["category"] for order in orders}),
        "frequency_tier": f"orders-{len(orders)}",
        "region": account.get("region"),
        "first_time": not orders,
    }


def _assert_profile_carries_no_identity(plain, secrets) -> None:
    """The frozen R5 scan — identity-shaped KEYS, then identity VALUES — on one profile.

    `test_buyer_profile_contains_no_identity_fields` runs this once, on one profile. The
    T-132 tests run it on every profile they build, because a build that varies with the
    population or the session must not leak on the seventeenth buyer either.
    """
    for key, _value in _walk(plain):
        assert not IDENTITY_KEY_RE.search(key), (
            f"R5: identity-shaped key {key!r} reached the store-facing BuyerProfile"
        )
    haystack = _blob(plain).lower()
    for secret in secrets:
        assert secret not in haystack, (
            f"R5: buyer identity value {secret!r} leaked into the BuyerProfile: {haystack}"
        )

@pytest.mark.epic("E7")
@pytest.mark.ticket("T-132")
def test_profile_buckets_are_k_anonymous_over_a_reference_population():
    """R5: a published bucket set covers >= K buyers, and still separates real cohorts.

    T-070 rotates the pseudonym correctly and the rotation buys nothing, because `buckets`
    is a pure function of the account: three pseudonyms for one buyer publish ONE identical
    bucket set, so any store that has seen that buyer once re-links every later session.
    The pseudonym rotates; the fingerprint underneath it does not.

    The guarantee is therefore a property of the CROWD, not of one buyer's variation, and it
    is pinned from both sides. No published bucket set may cover fewer than
    `PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY` buyers (privacy), and the population's coarse cohorts must stay
    separated (utility). Over `PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY * PROFILE_REFERENCE_COHORTS` buyers those
    two together admit exactly one shape — a partition into `PROFILE_REFERENCE_COHORTS`
    classes of `PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY` — so a profile that publishes nothing at all is
    rejected just as firmly as today's fingerprint.
    """
    from apps.buyer.svc.src.profile import build_profile

    population = _reference_population()
    assert len(population) == PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY * PROFILE_REFERENCE_COHORTS

    # Positive control: the measurement itself must be able to see a fingerprint. A
    # deliberately linkable publisher has to come back as singletons; if it does not, the
    # classing machinery is broken and a green verdict below would mean nothing.
    control = _equivalence_classes(_control_buckets, population)
    assert len(control) == len(population) and min(map(len, control.values())) == 1, (
        f"the equivalence-class machinery cannot see a fingerprint: a publisher that "
        f"republishes exact totals, exact order counts, the raw category set and the ISO "
        f"subdivision produced {len(control)} classes over {len(population)} buyers "
        f"(expected {len(population)} singletons). Fix the measurement before trusting "
        f"anything it says about the product."
    )

    def _publish(account, index):
        plain = _plain(build_profile(account, f"psn-t132pop-{index:022x}"))
        assert set(plain) == {"pseudonym", "buckets"}, (
            f"DESIGN pins BuyerProfile to exactly {{pseudonym, buckets}}, got {sorted(plain)}"
        )
        assert set(plain["buckets"]) == PROFILE_BUCKET_KEYS, (
            f"DESIGN pins the buckets to exactly {sorted(PROFILE_BUCKET_KEYS)}, got "
            f"{sorted(plain['buckets'])} — suppressing a rare facet must null its VALUE, "
            f"never drop its key: a missing key is itself a signal"
        )
        _assert_profile_carries_no_identity(plain, ("example.com", account["email"]))
        return plain["buckets"]

    classes = _equivalence_classes(_publish, population)
    rarest = min(classes, key=lambda vector: len(classes[vector]))
    assert len(classes[rarest]) >= PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY, (
        f"R5/T-132: the bucket set {rarest} is published by only {len(classes[rarest])} of "
        f"{len(population)} reference buyers ({classes[rarest]}). Those buyers differ only "
        f"in detail the buckets promise to coarsen away, so a store that has seen one of "
        f"them once re-links every later pseudonym of that buyer and the rotation buys "
        f"nothing. Every published bucket set must cover at least {PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY} "
        f"buyers."
    )
    assert len(classes) >= PROFILE_REFERENCE_COHORTS, (
        f"R5/T-132: the reference population holds {PROFILE_REFERENCE_COHORTS} coarse "
        f"cohorts — differing in frequency tier, budget band, region and order history — "
        f"and the profile published only {len(classes)} distinct bucket set(s). Anonymity "
        f"bought by suppressing a facet stores need is not the guarantee; it is the "
        f"surrender. Got {json.dumps(sorted(classes), indent=1)}"
    )


@pytest.mark.epic("E7")
@pytest.mark.ticket("T-132")
def test_category_affinity_is_a_closed_generalising_vocabulary():
    """R5/T-132: affinity terms come from a small closed vocabulary that actually generalises.

    `coarsen_categories` caps the COUNT of slugs and nothing else — no length cap, no
    vocabulary — so an arbitrary order-category string is slugged and published verbatim.
    That free-text slug is the high-entropy half of the linkage: two sessions both carrying
    `hand-forged-damascus-chef-knives-...` are the same buyer whatever the pseudonym says.
    It is also invisible to the identity backstop, which holds an account's OWN category
    slugs out of its haystack on purpose.

    A closed vocabulary is what closes both: a term chosen from a fixed table cannot be
    unique to one buyer and cannot spell one's name.
    """
    from apps.buyer.svc.src import profile as profile_module
    from apps.buyer.svc.src.profile import CATEGORY_VOCABULARY, build_profile

    vocabulary = frozenset(CATEGORY_VOCABULARY)
    assert 2 <= len(vocabulary) <= CATEGORY_VOCABULARY_MAX, (
        f"R5/T-132: the affinity vocabulary must be closed and small, got {len(vocabulary)} "
        f"terms: {sorted(vocabulary)}"
    )
    for term in vocabulary:
        assert isinstance(term, str) and _CATEGORY_TERM_RE.match(term), (
            f"R5: affinity vocabulary term {term!r} is not a lowercase slug"
        )
        assert len(term) <= CATEGORY_TERM_MAX_LEN, (
            f"R5: affinity term {term!r} is {len(term)} characters — a term that long "
            f"carries free text, which is the high-entropy half of re-linkage"
        )
    for term in vocabulary:
        for fragment in _T070_IDENTITY_VALUES:
            assert fragment not in term.lower(), (
                f"R5/T-132: the declared vocabulary carries the buyer identity fragment "
                f"{fragment!r} in term {term!r}. A table grown out of the accounts it "
                f"describes is a directory wearing a vocabulary's clothes."
            )

    def _affinity(*categories, tag="probe", email="probe@example.net"):
        account = {
            "email": email,
            "region": "US-OR",
            "orders": [
                {"order_ref": f"ord-{index}", "total": 120.0, "category": category}
                for index, category in enumerate(categories)
            ],
        }
        plain = _plain(build_profile(account, f"psn-t132voc-{tag}"))
        published = plain["buckets"]["category_affinity"]
        assert isinstance(published, list), (
            f"buckets['category_affinity'] is always a list; a withheld affinity is the "
            f"EMPTY list, never null (the frozen schema types it 'array'), got {published!r}"
        )
        assert set(published) <= vocabulary, (
            f"R5/T-132: order categories {categories!r} were published as {published!r}. A "
            f"term outside the closed vocabulary is a per-buyer fingerprint that survives "
            f"every pseudonym rotation."
        )
        assert len(published) <= CATEGORY_AFFINITY_MAX, (
            f"R5/T-132: {len(published)} affinity terms in one profile ({published!r}). A "
            f"longer list is a purchase log, and a purchase log is a fingerprint even when "
            f"every term in it is drawn from the closed vocabulary."
        )
        return published

    hostile = (
        "hand-forged damascus chef knives for left-handed bakers, batch 7734",
        "dana.reyes@example.com",
        "44 Alder Way, Portland OR 97205",
        "gift for Marcus - birthday 1987-04-02",
        "3f2b91c4-7d0e-4a55-9b21-6c8e4f0a1d33",
        "z" * 300,
    )
    for position, raw in enumerate(hostile):
        published = _affinity(raw, tag=f"hostile{position}")
        haystack = " ".join(published).lower()
        for word in set(_LEAKABLE_WORD_RE.findall(raw.lower())):
            assert word not in haystack, (
                f"R5/T-132: free text {word!r} out of the order category {raw[:60]!r} "
                f"reached the store-facing profile"
            )

    # A vocabulary that admits whatever it is shown is not closed, and membership against a
    # self-growing set is a guard that rejects nothing.
    assert frozenset(getattr(profile_module, "CATEGORY_VOCABULARY")) == vocabulary, (
        "R5/T-132: CATEGORY_VOCABULARY grew while profiles were being built"
    )

    # Membership against a handful of strings proves little. Sweep unrelated accounts.
    for index in range(CATEGORY_SWEEP_ACCOUNTS):
        _affinity(
            f"seed-{index:04d}-widget-{index * 7919:x}",
            tag=f"sweep{index:04d}",
            email=f"s{index}@example.net",
        )
    assert frozenset(getattr(profile_module, "CATEGORY_VOCABULARY")) == vocabulary, (
        f"R5/T-132: CATEGORY_VOCABULARY grew from {len(vocabulary)} to "
        f"{len(frozenset(profile_module.CATEGORY_VOCABULARY))} terms while "
        f"{CATEGORY_SWEEP_ACCOUNTS} unrelated accounts were published. A vocabulary that "
        f"interns whatever it is shown gives every buyer a permanent linkage key."
    )

    # It must GENERALISE, not allowlist its own inputs...
    siblings = _affinity(
        "running-shoes", "running-shoes", "trail-running-shoes", "trail-running-shoes",
        tag="siblings",
    )
    assert len(set(siblings)) == 1, (
        f"R5/T-132: two sibling categories must generalise to exactly ONE published term, "
        f"got {siblings!r} — keeping them apart leaves every buyer distinguishable, and "
        f"dropping both publishes nothing at all"
    )
    # ...and it must not buy its anonymity by mapping the world to one catch-all.
    assert _affinity("running-shoes", tag="shoes") != _affinity("face-serum", tag="serum"), (
        "R5/T-132: unrelated categories must stay distinguishable — a vocabulary that maps "
        "everything to one term is anonymity bought by publishing nothing"
    )

    # The ORDER of the list is a per-buyer signal of its own: `coarsen_categories` ranks by
    # purchase count, so two buyers holding the same terms are still told apart by which one
    # they buy most.
    ranked = _affinity("face-serum", "running-shoes", "running-shoes", tag="ranked")
    assert ranked == sorted(set(ranked)), (
        f"R5/T-132: the affinity list must be canonically ordered and de-duplicated, got "
        f"{ranked!r} — an order derived from purchase counts re-links a buyer even when "
        f"every term in the list is shared with a crowd"
    )

def test_rare_facets_are_suppressed_in_place_and_never_drop_a_bucket_key():
    """R5/T-132: suppression is a VALUE inside the pinned five keys, never a missing key.

    DESIGN pins `buckets` to exactly five keys, so a facet too rare to publish cannot be
    dropped — it has to be nulled in place (`[]` for the affinity list, which the frozen
    schema types as an array with no null branch). This test proves that is expressible, and
    it pins the free-text discipline on the OTHER two intake paths: `account["region"]` and
    `account["budget_band"]`, which are strings a buyer or an importer can put anything into.

    It also disposes of the one bucket that can never be suppressed. `first_time` is pinned
    to a bool by the frozen contract, so an implementation cannot null it; it must therefore
    carry no bit of its own, or it becomes an unsuppressible splitter of a k-class.
    """
    from apps.buyer.svc.src.profile import build_profile

    exotic = {
        "email": "solo@example.net",
        "region": "44 Alder Way, Portland OR 97205",
        "budget_band": "mid-range-ish",
        "orders": [
            {"order_ref": "ord-1", "total": 3.5, "category": "bespoke orrery restoration"}
        ],
    }
    buckets = _plain(build_profile(exotic, "psn-t132rare-" + "b" * 19))["buckets"]
    assert set(buckets) == PROFILE_BUCKET_KEYS, (
        f"R5: suppressing a rare facet must null it IN PLACE — DESIGN still pins the bucket "
        f"keys to exactly {sorted(PROFILE_BUCKET_KEYS)}, got {sorted(buckets)}"
    )
    assert isinstance(buckets["first_time"], bool)
    assert isinstance(buckets["category_affinity"], list)
    haystack = _blob(buckets).lower()
    for rare in ("alder", "portland", "97205", "orrery", "bespoke", "mid-range-ish"):
        assert rare not in haystack, (
            f"R5/T-132: rare free-text value {rare!r} survived into the published buckets: "
            f"{haystack}. A value nobody else can publish is a permanent linkage key."
        )

    fresh = _plain(build_profile({"email": "new@example.net"}, "psn-t132rare-" + "c" * 19))
    settled = _plain(
        build_profile(
            {
                "email": "old@example.net",
                "region": "US-OR",
                "orders": [{"order_ref": "o", "total": 120.0, "category": "running-shoes"}],
            },
            "psn-t132rare-" + "d" * 19,
        )
    )
    assert set(fresh["buckets"]) == PROFILE_BUCKET_KEYS
    assert set(settled["buckets"]) == PROFILE_BUCKET_KEYS
    assert fresh["buckets"]["first_time"] is True
    assert settled["buckets"]["first_time"] is False
    assert fresh["buckets"]["frequency_tier"] != settled["buckets"]["frequency_tier"], (
        f"R5/T-132: `first_time` is the one bucket the frozen contract forbids nulling, so "
        f"it must carry no information of its own — it has to be redundant with the "
        f"zero-order frequency tier, or it splits a k-class with no remedy. Got tier "
        f"{fresh['buckets']['frequency_tier']!r} for a buyer with no orders and "
        f"{settled['buckets']['frequency_tier']!r} for a buyer with one."
    )

def test_rotating_a_pseudonym_lands_the_buyer_in_a_crowd_not_on_themselves():

    test joins the two halves: the pseudonym rotates AND the fingerprint under it is a crowd,
    measured as the store's own re-link confidence of 1-in-len(crowd).
    """

    from apps.buyer.svc.src.vault import PseudonymVault

    population = _reference_population()
    anchor = population[6]

@pytest.mark.ticket("T-132")
def test_profile_buckets_are_k_anonymous_over_a_reference_population():
    """R5: a published bucket set covers >= K buyers, and still separates real cohorts.

    T-070 rotates the pseudonym correctly and the rotation buys nothing, because `buckets`
    is a pure function of the account: three pseudonyms for one buyer publish ONE identical
    bucket set, so any store that has seen that buyer once re-links every later session.
    The pseudonym rotates; the fingerprint underneath it does not.

    The guarantee is therefore a property of the CROWD, not of one buyer's variation, and it
    is pinned from both sides. No published bucket set may cover fewer than
    `PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY` buyers (privacy), and the population's coarse cohorts must stay
    separated (utility). Over `PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY * PROFILE_REFERENCE_COHORTS` buyers those
    two together admit exactly one shape — a partition into `PROFILE_REFERENCE_COHORTS`
    classes of `PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY` — so a profile that publishes nothing at all is
    rejected just as firmly as today's fingerprint.
    """
    from apps.buyer.svc.src.profile import build_profile

    population = _reference_population()
    assert len(population) == PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY * PROFILE_REFERENCE_COHORTS

    # Positive control: the measurement itself must be able to see a fingerprint. A
    # deliberately linkable publisher has to come back as singletons; if it does not, the
    # classing machinery is broken and a green verdict below would mean nothing.
    control = _equivalence_classes(_control_buckets, population)
    assert len(control) == len(population) and min(map(len, control.values())) == 1, (
        f"the equivalence-class machinery cannot see a fingerprint: a publisher that "
        f"republishes exact totals, exact order counts, the raw category set and the ISO "
        f"subdivision produced {len(control)} classes over {len(population)} buyers "
        f"(expected {len(population)} singletons). Fix the measurement before trusting "
        f"anything it says about the product."
    )

    def _publish(account, index):
        plain = _plain(build_profile(account, f"psn-t132pop-{index:022x}"))
        assert set(plain) == {"pseudonym", "buckets"}, (
            f"DESIGN pins BuyerProfile to exactly {{pseudonym, buckets}}, got {sorted(plain)}"
        )
        assert set(plain["buckets"]) == PROFILE_BUCKET_KEYS, (
            f"DESIGN pins the buckets to exactly {sorted(PROFILE_BUCKET_KEYS)}, got "
            f"{sorted(plain['buckets'])} — suppressing a rare facet must null its VALUE, "
            f"never drop its key: a missing key is itself a signal"
        )
        _assert_profile_carries_no_identity(plain, ("example.com", account["email"]))
        return plain["buckets"]

    classes = _equivalence_classes(_publish, population)
    rarest = min(classes, key=lambda vector: len(classes[vector]))
    assert len(classes[rarest]) >= PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY, (
        f"R5/T-132: the bucket set {rarest} is published by only {len(classes[rarest])} of "
        f"{len(population)} reference buyers ({classes[rarest]}). Those buyers differ only "
        f"in detail the buckets promise to coarsen away, so a store that has seen one of "
        f"them once re-links every later pseudonym of that buyer and the rotation buys "
        f"nothing. Every published bucket set must cover at least {PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY} "
        f"buyers."
    )
    assert len(classes) >= PROFILE_REFERENCE_COHORTS, (
        f"R5/T-132: the reference population holds {PROFILE_REFERENCE_COHORTS} coarse "
        f"cohorts — differing in frequency tier, budget band, region and order history — "
        f"and the profile published only {len(classes)} distinct bucket set(s). Anonymity "
        f"bought by suppressing a facet stores need is not the guarantee; it is the "
        f"surrender. Got {json.dumps(sorted(classes), indent=1)}"

@pytest.mark.epic("E7")
@pytest.mark.ticket("T-132")
def test_category_affinity_is_a_closed_generalising_vocabulary():
    """R5/T-132: affinity terms come from a small closed vocabulary that actually generalises.

    `coarsen_categories` caps the COUNT of slugs and nothing else — no length cap, no
    vocabulary — so an arbitrary order-category string is slugged and published verbatim.
    That free-text slug is the high-entropy half of the linkage: two sessions both carrying
    `hand-forged-damascus-chef-knives-...` are the same buyer whatever the pseudonym says.
    It is also invisible to the identity backstop, which holds an account's OWN category
    slugs out of its haystack on purpose.

    A closed vocabulary is what closes both: a term chosen from a fixed table cannot be
    unique to one buyer and cannot spell one's name.
    """
    from apps.buyer.svc.src import profile as profile_module
    from apps.buyer.svc.src.profile import CATEGORY_VOCABULARY, build_profile

    vocabulary = frozenset(CATEGORY_VOCABULARY)
    assert 2 <= len(vocabulary) <= CATEGORY_VOCABULARY_MAX, (
        f"R5/T-132: the affinity vocabulary must be closed and small, got {len(vocabulary)} "
        f"terms: {sorted(vocabulary)}"
    )
    for term in vocabulary:
        assert isinstance(term, str) and _CATEGORY_TERM_RE.match(term), (
            f"R5: affinity vocabulary term {term!r} is not a lowercase slug"
        )
        assert len(term) <= CATEGORY_TERM_MAX_LEN, (
            f"R5: affinity term {term!r} is {len(term)} characters — a term that long "
            f"carries free text, which is the high-entropy half of re-linkage"
        )
    for term in vocabulary:
        for fragment in _T070_IDENTITY_VALUES:
            assert fragment not in term.lower(), (
                f"R5/T-132: the declared vocabulary carries the buyer identity fragment "
                f"{fragment!r} in term {term!r}. A table grown out of the accounts it "
                f"describes is a directory wearing a vocabulary's clothes."
            )

    def _affinity(*categories, tag="probe", email="probe@example.net"):
        account = {
            "email": email,
            "region": "US-OR",
            "orders": [
                {"order_ref": f"ord-{index}", "total": 120.0, "category": category}
                for index, category in enumerate(categories)
            ],
        }
        plain = _plain(build_profile(account, f"psn-t132voc-{tag}"))
        published = plain["buckets"]["category_affinity"]
        assert isinstance(published, list), (
            f"buckets['category_affinity'] is always a list; a withheld affinity is the "
            f"EMPTY list, never null (the frozen schema types it 'array'), got {published!r}"
        )
        assert set(published) <= vocabulary, (
            f"R5/T-132: order categories {categories!r} were published as {published!r}. A "
            f"term outside the closed vocabulary is a per-buyer fingerprint that survives "
            f"every pseudonym rotation."
        )
        assert len(published) <= CATEGORY_AFFINITY_MAX, (
            f"R5/T-132: {len(published)} affinity terms in one profile ({published!r}). A "
            f"longer list is a purchase log, and a purchase log is a fingerprint even when "
            f"every term in it is drawn from the closed vocabulary."
        )
        return published

    hostile = (
        "hand-forged damascus chef knives for left-handed bakers, batch 7734",
        "dana.reyes@example.com",
        "44 Alder Way, Portland OR 97205",
        "gift for Marcus - birthday 1987-04-02",
        "3f2b91c4-7d0e-4a55-9b21-6c8e4f0a1d33",
        "z" * 300,
    )
    for position, raw in enumerate(hostile):
        published = _affinity(raw, tag=f"hostile{position}")
        haystack = " ".join(published).lower()
        for word in set(_LEAKABLE_WORD_RE.findall(raw.lower())):
            assert word not in haystack, (
                f"R5/T-132: free text {word!r} out of the order category {raw[:60]!r} "
                f"reached the store-facing profile"
            )

    # A vocabulary that admits whatever it is shown is not closed, and membership against a
    # self-growing set is a guard that rejects nothing.
    assert frozenset(getattr(profile_module, "CATEGORY_VOCABULARY")) == vocabulary, (
        "R5/T-132: CATEGORY_VOCABULARY grew while profiles were being built"
    )

    # Membership against a handful of strings proves little. Sweep unrelated accounts.
    for index in range(CATEGORY_SWEEP_ACCOUNTS):
        _affinity(
            f"seed-{index:04d}-widget-{index * 7919:x}",
            tag=f"sweep{index:04d}",
            email=f"s{index}@example.net",
        )
    assert frozenset(getattr(profile_module, "CATEGORY_VOCABULARY")) == vocabulary, (
        f"R5/T-132: CATEGORY_VOCABULARY grew from {len(vocabulary)} to "
        f"{len(frozenset(profile_module.CATEGORY_VOCABULARY))} terms while "
        f"{CATEGORY_SWEEP_ACCOUNTS} unrelated accounts were published. A vocabulary that "
        f"interns whatever it is shown gives every buyer a permanent linkage key."
    )

    # It must GENERALISE, not allowlist its own inputs...
    siblings = _affinity(
        "running-shoes", "running-shoes", "trail-running-shoes", "trail-running-shoes",
        tag="siblings",
    )
    assert len(set(siblings)) == 1, (
        f"R5/T-132: two sibling categories must generalise to exactly ONE published term, "
        f"got {siblings!r} — keeping them apart leaves every buyer distinguishable, and "
        f"dropping both publishes nothing at all"
    )
    # ...and it must not buy its anonymity by mapping the world to one catch-all.
    assert _affinity("running-shoes", tag="shoes") != _affinity("face-serum", tag="serum"), (
        "R5/T-132: unrelated categories must stay distinguishable — a vocabulary that maps "
        "everything to one term is anonymity bought by publishing nothing"
    )

    # The ORDER of the list is a per-buyer signal of its own: `coarsen_categories` ranks by
    # purchase count, so two buyers holding the same terms are still told apart by which one
    # they buy most.
    ranked = _affinity("face-serum", "running-shoes", "running-shoes", tag="ranked")
    assert ranked == sorted(set(ranked)), (
        f"R5/T-132: the affinity list must be canonically ordered and de-duplicated, got "
        f"{ranked!r} — an order derived from purchase counts re-links a buyer even when "
        f"every term in the list is shared with a crowd"
    )

spec.freeze_log_reason:
Amendment 4, user-approved (T-132, severity HIGH; the third amendment to touch the acceptance suite). T-070's R5 guarantee was HALF-TESTED: test_pseudonym_rotates_per_session_and_is_never_reissued pins that the pseudonym is fresh every session and never reissued, and NOTHING in the frozen suite asked whether the rotation buys the buyer anything. It does not. `buckets` is a pure function of the account, so successive pseudonyms publish byte-identical profiles — reproduced here at 8 rotations: 8 distinct pseudonyms, ONE bucket blob, {"budget_band": "100-250", "category_affinity": ["running-shoes", "trail-gear"], "first_time": false, "frequency_tier": "regular", "region": "US-OR"} — and any store that has seen a buyer once re-links every later session. Contributing factor, also reproduced: `coarsen_categories` caps the COUNT of slugs and nothing else, so the order category "hand-forged damascus chef knives for left-handed bakers, batch 7734" ships to stores as a single 66-character free-text slug, and `build_profile` RETURNS it rather than raising IdentityLeak because `_incidental_bucket_values` holds an account's own category slugs out of the leak haystack on purpose.

Fix: FOUR TESTS ADDED, NOTHING RELAXED. First it was verified — by execution, not inspection — that the frozen contract never blocked the fix: ProfileBuckets already types budget_band/frequency_tier/region as `str | None` and category_affinity as an array defaulting to [], so suppression and generalisation are expressible as VALUES inside the five pinned keys, and both frozen T-070 tests are blind to the change. The suite now measures the guarantee as what it actually is — a property of the CROWD, not of one buyer's session-to-session variation. A 30-buyer reference population in 6 cohorts of 5 is built into the file; every published bucket set must cover at least K=5 buyers (privacy floor) AND the 6 coarse cohorts must stay separated (utility floor), which over 30 buyers admits exactly one shape and rejects the publish-nothing cheat as firmly as today's fingerprint. `category_affinity` is required to draw from a small, declared, non-growing CATEGORY_VOCABULARY that demonstrably generalises (siblings merge to one term, unrelated categories stay apart, the list is canonically ordered because the shipped frequency ranking leaks purchase counts). Suppression must null a facet IN PLACE, never drop a key, and `first_time` — the one bucket the frozen contract forbids nulling — must be redundant with the zero-order frequency tier so it cannot split a k-class with no remedy. Three grafts carry their own weight: a POSITIVE CONTROL (a deliberately linkable publisher must come back as 30 singletons before the k measurement is trusted, so "the attack found nothing" and "the attack is broken" cannot be the same green), a 200-account cross-account sweep (which is what rejects "truncate the free text and call it a bucket"), and the frozen identity-key/identity-value scan now run on every profile the new tests build rather than on one — a strict STRENGTHENING of assertions this amendment was forbidden to remove.

VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS BEFORE RE-FREEZING, the Amendment 2 standard. RED as shipped: all four fail against the T-070 code for four independent reasons — a bucket set published by 1 of 30 reference buyers; ImportError on CATEGORY_VOCABULARY; the rare slug 'bespoke-orrery-restoration' surviving into the published buckets; and a crowd of 1, i.e. re-link confidence 1-in-1. GREEN when earned: against a prototype generaliser (closed 12-term vocabulary via a keyword hierarchy, region generalised one level up, canonical sorted/de-duplicated affinity, the vocabulary folded into _CLOSED_VOCABULARY) all four pass, and the population resolves to 6 classes of exactly 5. So the amendment makes R5's unlinkability half reachable WITHOUT MAKING IT FREE. Six sabotages run, six caught: publish-nothing (fails the utility floor at 2 classes and the first_time redundancy), constant-profile (1 class), per-session noise (3 wandering vectors and the population re-fragmented to singletons), the PARTIAL fix that closes the vocabulary but leaves region at ISO subdivision (still 1-in-1 — so the contributing factor alone does not buy the amendment), a self-interning vocabulary (39 terms), and a neutered measurement (the positive control fires first).

WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: no assertion weakened, no pin relaxed, no test renamed, removed, or re-marked; contract_changes is empty. test_buyer_profile_contains_no_identity_fields and test_pseudonym_rotates_per_session_and_is_never_reissued are byte-identical before and after and PASS in both directions (2 passed against the shipped code, 2 passed against the prototype fix) — that is the evidence behind claiming zero contract changes rather than assuming it. Baseline vs amended on identical code: 7 failed/2 passed -> 11 failed/2 passed, exactly +4 red and +0 green. Suite 120 -> 124; acceptance_collected target 120 -> 124 and e7_buyer_passing target 9 -> 13 move in this same edit. acceptance_pass_rate falls 13.33 (16/120) -> 12.90 (16/124) because an unmet guarantee must read as unmet. Only test_e7_buyer.py and goals.json changed.

TWO THINGS RECORDED RATHER THAN FIXED HERE. (1) SPEC.md:14 R5 promises "a rotating pseudonym and a coarsened profile" and DESIGN.md:55 promises "no identity fields; pseudonym rotates per session" — NEITHER promises that two sessions of one buyer cannot be linked. This amendment therefore ADDS a promise, and must be paired with a SPEC/DESIGN edit or the suite scores something the docs do not ask for; the added promise is per-buyer recoding granularity and is distinct from SPEC.md:56's k-anonymity non-goal, which A6 scopes to shortlist slot composition. (2) The guarantee is enforced against a reference population baked into the suite, not against the live buyer base — `build_profile(account, pseudonym)` cannot see a population, so what these tests pin is "the coarsening is coarse enough that buyers differing only below its granularity are indistinguishable, and coarse-cohort separation survives", NOT "k=5 in production". A cohort-count index in vault.* with suppression until the live class reaches k is a second ticket and would be an additive keyword argument, never a change to the frozen 2-arg call.
spec.implementation_brief:
TICKET: T-132 — make the T-070 unlinkability guarantee real. SCOPE: apps/buyer/** only. The four new frozen tests in .swarm-loop/acceptance/test_e7_buyer.py define done; you may not edit them.

WHAT IS BROKEN. `buckets` is a pure function of the account, so a rotated pseudonym publishes a byte-identical fingerprint (reproduced: 8 pseudonyms, 1 bucket blob). Fix it by GENERALISATION — coarser but TRUE values, deterministic in the account — not by per-session noise. The frozen suite forbids noise explicitly (test_rotating_a_pseudonym... asserts the 3 rotations publish ONE bucket set) and forbids demolition explicitly (the utility floor requires 6 distinct classes over the reference population). Stores must be able to bid on what you publish.

FOUR CHANGES, ALL IN apps/buyer/svc/src/profile/__init__.py:

1. DECLARE `CATEGORY_VOCABULARY` — a module-level frozenset of 2..24 short lowercase slugs (^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$, <= 24 chars), hand-written, containing no buyer identity fragment. Add it to __all__. It must be IMMUTABLE: the suite snapshots it, publishes 200+ profiles, and asserts it has not grown. A vocabulary that interns whatever it is shown is a guard that rejects nothing.

2. REWRITE `coarsen_categories` as a GENERALISATION HIERARCHY, not an allowlist. Map each order category into a parent term by keyword; anything unrecognised becomes the designated catch-all. Two required properties, both tested: sibling categories ("running-shoes" and "trail-running-shoes") must collapse to ONE term, and unrelated categories ("running-shoes" vs "face-serum") must NOT collapse together. Then DEDUPE and SORT canonically, keeping the existing CATEGORY_LIMIT of 3. The shipped `sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda i: (-i[1], i[0]))` ranks by purchase count and therefore re-links a buyer through list ORDER even when every term is shared — that ordering must go.

3. GENERALISE `coarsen_region` one level up. `US-OR` -> `US` (or a continental zone; the population contains three countries on three continents and does not rule on which). It must still refuse a street address and a postal code — do not weaken what is already there. THIS IS NOT OPTIONAL: the sabotage that closes the vocabulary and leaves region at ISO subdivision still fails two of the four tests at 1-in-1 re-linkage.

4. FOLD THE VOCABULARY INTO `_CLOSED_VOCABULARY`. A generalised term ("footwear") is chosen from a fixed table and was never copied off the account, so it must be held out of the `identity_leaks` haystack alongside the bands and tiers. Skip this and `identity_leaks` fails CLOSED — a denial of service — on any buyer whose name or address word collides with a bucket label. That failure mode is exactly why `_incidental_bucket_values` was written; extend it, do not bypass it.

TWO TRAPS, BOTH VERIFIED IN THE REPO:
 - ENFORCE THE VOCABULARY IN THE BUILDER, NEVER IN THE CONTRACT MODEL. A pydantic validator on ProfileBuckets in packages/contracts/generated/python/protocol.py would take frozen E1 and E4 tests red: test_e1_foundation.py:218 constructs buckets with budget_band "40-80" and category_affinity ["skincare"], test_e4_store_agent.py:326 with "50-150" and ["outerwear"]. Turning a T-132 fix into an E1/E4 regression is not a fix.
 - `first_time` IS PINNED TO A BOOL by the frozen contract, so it can never be suppressed. It must therefore stay redundant with the zero-order frequency tier (True exactly when the tier is the zero tier) or it becomes an unsuppressible splitter of a k-class. Do not null frequency_tier for everyone: that is precisely what the publish-nothing sabotage did, and the suite caught it there.

DO NOT: introduce per-session randomness of any kind; make `build_profile` non-deterministic (`publish_profile` writes one row per pseudonym into app.buyer_accounts and a wandering profile would grow that table per session); add a sixth bucket key (ProfileBuckets is extra="forbid" and frozen E1/E4 payloads pin the five); publish a value that is not this buyer's.

HOW TO KNOW YOU ARE DONE: PROXYSHOP_WORKER=<your worker> ./.venv/bin/python -m pytest .swarm-loop/acceptance/test_e7_buyer.py -k "T-132 or profile_contains or pseudonym_rotates" must show 6 passed — the four T-132 tests AND both frozen T-070 tests. Before you claim it, run these four fakes against your fix and confirm every one is REJECTED: (a) null every bucket; (b) one constant profile for all buyers; (c) append a per-session nonce term to the affinity list; (d) your vocabulary work with `coarsen_region` left untouched. All four were run against the amended suite and all four were caught.

FILED SEPARATELY, NOT YOURS TO CARRY: `_incidental_bucket_values()` deliberately whitelists THIS account's own order-category slugs out of the identity_leaks haystack, so identity text routed through orders[].category ships to stores with the backstop's blessing — verified live, build_profile returned a profile containing 'dana', 'reyes', 'alder way' and '97205' inside category_affinity and did not raise. Your closed vocabulary closes that hole as a side effect, but nothing forces the now-redundant whitelist to be REMOVED, and it silently re-opens if free text ever returns to that bucket. That deserves its own ticket. Also owed alongside this ticket: the paired SPEC.md:14 / DESIGN.md:55 edits, since neither doc currently promises unlinkability at all.

findings.problem: REFUTED BY CONSTRUCTION. A degenerate `build_buckets` passes all four new T-132 tests AND both frozen T-070 tests (6 passed) while leaving buyers essentially as re-linkable as the shipped defect. The k floor is measured only against the 30-account `_reference_population()` baked into the test file, and that fixture exercises a tiny corner of every coarsener's input domain: exactly 3 budget bands ("100-250", "1000+", None), 3 frequency tiers (max 9 orders, so "frequent" is never reached), 3 countries (US-*, DE-*, and bare "JP"), and 2 distinct category strings per buyer. Every facet value OUTSIDE that window is completely unconstrained, so an implementation can generalise exactly where the fixture looks and fingerprint everywhere else.
findings.evidence: Executed, not reasoned. Amended suite assembled verbatim at /private/tmp/t132refute/test_e7_amended.py (frozen file + the amendment's three edits; anchors verified unique). Baseline against shipped code in the f1-buyer worktree reproduces the amendment's own claim exactly: `4 failed, 2 passed` with `AssertionError: ... shared by only 1 of 30 reference buyers (['b1@example.com']), confidence 1-in-1`. Degenerate implementation at /private/tmp/t132refute/degenerate.py (monkeypatches module attrs on apps/buyer/svc/src/profile/__init__.py; no repo file edited): closed 24-term hand-written non-growing CATEGORY_VOCABULARY, keyword rules only for the two relationships the suite probes, unrecognised categories hashed by first token into the vocabulary, `budget_band` coarse in [100,250) and >=1000 and unit-wide elsewhere, `frequency_tier` coarse to 9 orders and the exact count above, `coarsen_region` rolled up only for the three 'launch markets' US/DE/JP and ISO-verbatim otherwise. Result: `6 passed, 7 deselected`. Re-linkability on 4,000 synthetic buyers (16 countries x 8 ISO subdivisions, order counts 0-40, six spend scales, 36 real category strings; /private/tmp/t132refute/measure.py): SHIPPED 3868 classes / 94.8% of buyers in a crowd of ONE / 99.3% in a crowd < 5. DEGENERATE 3805 classes / 92.8% crowd-of-one / 98.1% in a crowd < 5. The amended suite certifies a 2-point improvement as the guarantee being met.
findings.suggested_repair: Close the vocabulary for the other three value-bearing buckets, the way the amendment closes it for `category_affinity` — this is the single highest-value change and it kills three of the four channels outright. Add to the vocabulary test (or a fifth test): `coarsen_region` output must be drawn from a declared module-level closed `REGION_VOCABULARY` (assert non-growing across the same 200-account sweep, and assert two subdivisions of an ARBITRARY country not in the fixture collapse to one term); `coarsen_budget_band` output must be in `{label for BUDGET_BANDS} | {TOP_BUDGET_BAND, None}`; `coarsen_frequency_tier` output must be in `{tier for FREQUENCY_TIERS}`. Then replace the hand-built 30-account fixture with a GENERATED population that spans each coarsener's whole domain (every band boundary, order counts crossing every tier including >9 and >100, >=8 countries with subdivisions including ones no launch-market list would contain, categories drawn from a taxonomy plus arbitrary free text) and assert min class size >= K over it. Finally add the missing CEILING: `len(classes) <= len(population) // PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY`. The suite currently has a floor on class count (utility) and no ceiling, so unbounded fragmentation outside the fixture is legal; the ceiling over a large generated population rejects all four channels in one assertion.

findings.problem: Each degenerate channel passes the amended suite ON ITS OWN, and each is an ordinary partial implementation rather than a contrived hardcode. "We only have region rollup tables for our launch markets", "keep the exact order count for high-volume buyers", and "hash unrecognised categories into the vocabulary instead of a single catch-all" are all things a competent implementer writes without any intent to cheat — and each one alone defeats the guarantee while the suite reports it met. The amendment's REQUIRED sabotage list contains no fake of this shape: all five listed sabotages either publish nothing, publish a constant, add per-session noise, self-intern the vocabulary, or leave region wholly untouched. The one that comes closest (sabotage D) is caught only because it leaves region at full ISO for the fixture's own US-*/DE-* buyers.
findings.evidence:
/private/tmp/t132refute/variant_plugin.py, each variant layered on an otherwise-honest generaliser, run against the amended suite with PROXYSHOP_WORKER=20:
  honest        : 6 passed   -> 58.2% of 4,000 buyers uniquely identified
  region        : 6 passed   -> 78.3% uniquely identified, 95.3% in a crowd < 5
  band          : 6 passed   -> 78.4% uniquely identified, 89.1% in a crowd < 5
  tier          : 6 passed   -> 67.1% uniquely identified, 92.7% in a crowd < 5
  cats          : 6 passed   -> 63.7% uniquely identified, 88.0% in a crowd < 5
For contrast, the amendment's own two structural sabotages ARE caught, as it claims: sab_nothing `3 failed, 3 passed`, sab_constant `3 failed, 3 passed`. The mechanism for the region channel is visible in `_reference_population()` itself: cohort E is `("JP", "JP", "JP", "JP", "JP")` — a bare country code with no subdivision — so cohort E cannot distinguish 'generalise to country' from 'pass through verbatim'. Only cohorts B/C (US-*) and D (DE-*) force a rollup, i.e. the population pins region generalisation for exactly two country prefixes.
findings.suggested_repair: Add the region/band/tier closed-vocabulary assertions from finding 1, and add these three fakes to `sabotage_checks` as REQUIRED, since they are the ones that currently survive: (a) generalise region only for a hardcoded set of countries and pass ISO subdivisions through for the rest; (b) publish the exact order count above the top tier's ceiling; (c) publish a fine-grained band outside the ranges the fixture exercises. A sabotage list that contains only demolition and noise is testing the two failure modes the tests were designed around; the interesting fakes are the ones that generalise correctly on the fixture and nowhere else.

findings.problem: The amendment's own GREEN reference implementation does not deliver the guarantee it certifies. The suite therefore cannot distinguish 'T-132 fixed' from 'T-132 still largely present' even for the intended fix — a green run is not evidence for the claim the failure messages make ("a store re-links every later pseudonym with confidence 1-in-N ... R5 requires at most 1-in-5"). This is the deeper problem: it is not only that a cheat passes, it is that passing means almost nothing about the property.
findings.evidence: Reconstruction of the prototype described in `expected_state_after_fix` and `implementation_brief` (closed keyword-hierarchy vocabulary with an `other` catch-all, `coarsen_region` generalised one level up to country, map-then-dedupe-then-sort under CATEGORY_LIMIT=3, shipped BUDGET_BANDS and FREQUENCY_TIERS unchanged), measured on the same 4,000-buyer population: 2787 equivalence classes, 58.2% of buyers in a crowd of ONE, 79.2% in a crowd smaller than 5. It scores `6 passed` on the amended suite. The amendment states the population then 'resolves to 6 classes of exactly 5' — true of the 30-account fixture, and not true of any population with more than three countries or a spend distribution wider than two bands. Note the shipped BUDGET_BANDS/FREQUENCY_TIERS are already coarse and already closed; the residual entropy comes from their CROSS PRODUCT with region and a 3-of-N affinity list, which no assertion bounds.
findings.suggested_repair: Assert the joint quantity, not the per-facet ones. Over a generated population of a few hundred buyers spanning the full domain, assert both `min(class sizes) >= PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY` and `len(classes) <= len(population) // PROFILE_K_ANONYMITY`. That is the only assertion shape that forces the coarsening to be coarse enough as a whole rather than facet by facet, and it is what makes the reference fix have to actually be a fix (it will fail as written — which is correct, and is Amendment 1's recorded standard: an unmet guarantee must read as unmet). Separately, cap the claim in `freeze_log_reason`: the second 'recorded rather than fixed' note already concedes the fixture-vs-production gap, but the failure messages inside the tests state a production-strength claim ('confidence 1-in-N', 'R5 requires at most 1-in-5') that the tests do not measure. Bring the message text down to what is measured.

findings.problem: `test_rare_facets_are_suppressed_in_place_and_never_drop_a_bucket_key` does NOT establish that `first_time` is redundant, contradicting the amendment's explicit claim that it 'disposes of the one bucket that can never be suppressed'. The assertion `fresh["frequency_tier"] != settled["frequency_tier"]` rejects only an implementation whose zero-order and one-order tiers collide. It admits an implementation where `first_time` carries a second, independent, unsuppressible bit — exactly the k-class splitter the docstring says it rules out.
findings.evidence: /private/tmp/t132refute/ft_plugin.py sets `first_time = (not orders) or bool(account.get("loyalty_id"))`, on top of the otherwise-honest generaliser. No account in `_reference_population()`, `_t070_account()`, or any probe in the four new tests carries a `loyalty_id` key, so on the fixture the extra bit is always False and every assertion holds: `6 passed, 7 deselected`. In production that bit splits every k-class in two and, being pinned to a bool by the frozen contract, can never be nulled — which is precisely the harm the test's docstring claims to have disposed of.
findings.suggested_repair: Assert the redundancy directly instead of inferring it from one pair of unequal tiers. Declare the zero-order tier as a module constant and assert, for every profile built by all four T-132 tests (the reference population, the 200-account sweep, and the probes): `buckets["first_time"] == (buckets["frequency_tier"] == ZERO_ORDER_TIER)`. That rejects any first_time carrying a bit of its own and admits exactly the redundant implementation the amendment intends.

findings.problem: `CATEGORY_AFFINITY_MAX = 3` drawn from a vocabulary of up to `CATEGORY_VOCABULARY_MAX = 24` admits 2,325 distinct published affinity sets. The constant's own docstring rejects 8-of-24 as 'over 700,000 distinct lists, which is a fingerprint again' but does not apply the same arithmetic to the limit it actually sets. Nothing in the amendment bounds the joint entropy of the five-value vector, so a fully compliant implementation can publish more distinct bucket sets than a real buyer base has crowds.
findings.evidence: C(24,3)+C(24,2)+24+1 = 2325 affinity sets. Multiplied by 6 budget bands, 4 frequency tiers and any plausible region vocabulary, the published vector space is 10^5-10^6 — far beyond a k=5 partition of any realistic population. Measured consequence: the 'ONLY 24-way hashed catch-all' variant (which is fully vocabulary-compliant — closed, non-growing, all terms <=24 chars, siblings merged, unrelated terms kept apart) raises unique-buyer rate from 58.2% to 63.7% and still scores `6 passed`.
findings.suggested_repair: Either lower `CATEGORY_VOCABULARY_MAX` and `CATEGORY_AFFINITY_MAX` so the affinity space is small by construction, or — better — let them stand and enforce the class-count ceiling from finding 1 over a generated population, which bounds the joint entropy directly and lets the implementer choose where to spend it. Also state the utility tradeoff in the amendment: the current text names the tradeoff for suppression ('a profile carrying less information is less useful') but the design as specified never actually forces any information out of the profile beyond the fixture's own facets.

findings.problem: The 200-account `CATEGORY_SWEEP_ACCOUNTS` sweep is weaker than the amendment claims. The only utility pressure on the vocabulary is the single assertion _affinity('running-shoes') != _affinity('face-serum'), which one keyword rule satisfies. The amendment's claim that it rejects 'anonymity bought by publishing nothing' for the affinity bucket is therefore true only to within one term.
findings.evidence: Run 1 (minimal vocab {footwear,other} + region->country, sorted): '6 passed, 7 deselected'. Run 2 (same 2-term vocab, affinity list frequency-ranked via sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda i: (-i[1], i[0]))): '6 passed, 7 deselected'. Run 3 (12-term vocab, same frequency ranking): 'FAILED test_category_affinity_is_a_closed_generalising_vocabulary' at the `ranked == sorted(set(ranked))` assertion, 1 failed 3 passed. All three run against apps/buyer/svc/src/profile in the f1-buyer worktree via a pytest plugin, PROXYSHOP_WORKER=23.
findings.suggested_repair: (a) Make the ordering probe vocabulary-independent: assert on a pair where the MORE-bought term must sort AFTER the less-bought one, e.g. require that for some input the published list is not in frequency order — or simpler, assert the published list is unchanged when the input orders are permuted and duplicated, which catches any count-derived ordering regardless of which terms are chosen. (b) Add a real coverage floor for the vocabulary so a one-bit taxonomy is rejected: require that a fixed corpus of, say, 12 plainly-unrelated categories (running-shoes, face-serum, chef-knife, winter-jacket, laptop, dog-food, ...) maps onto at least 4 distinct terms. (c) Make affinity load-bearing in the k test by adding a seventh cohort that differs from cohort b ONLY in order category, so a vocabulary that maps everything to one catch-all fails the utility floor instead of passing it.

findings.problem: The hostile free-text scan is a false-positive guard: it rejects legitimate closed vocabularies. For each hostile order-category string it asserts that no 4+ character lowercase alphanumeric word of the INPUT appears as a substring of any published term. But a keyword-driven generalisation hierarchy naturally maps a child to a parent that shares its stem. Measured: a perfectly legitimate 7-term closed vocabulary containing 'gifts', with the rule 'gift' -> 'gifts', fails on hostile[3] with `assert 'gift' not in 'gifts'`. The same trap awaits 'handbags' (hand), 'batch'-anything, 'bakery' (baker(s) is 6 chars), and any term sharing a stem with a probe word. This adds no privacy power that membership does not already provide — a term drawn from a snapshotted, size-capped, verified-non-growing vocabulary is by construction not free text copied off the account — so the assertion's only measurable effect is to reject correct implementations, inside a tolerance-0 frozen suite that cannot be edited afterwards.
findings.evidence: Plugin with VOCAB = {footwear, apparel, outdoor, beauty, kitchen, gifts, other} and KEYWORDS including ('gift','gifts'): "AssertionError: R5/T-132: free text 'gift' out of the order category 'gift for Marcus - birthday 1987-04-02' reached the store-facing profile / assert 'gift' not in 'gifts' / 'gift' is contained here: gifts". 1 failed, 12 deselected.
findings.suggested_repair: Delete the substring scan (membership in the snapshotted vocabulary strictly subsumes it), or narrow it so it only fires on words that are NOT accounted for by the declared vocabulary — e.g. skip any input word that is a substring of a term already present in CATEGORY_VOCABULARY before the profiles were built. If the intent is 'no term was invented from this input', assert that instead: the published set must be a subset of the vocabulary snapshot taken before any profile was built, which the test already does.

findings.problem: The amendment introduces a nondeterministic failure into a tolerance-0 frozen metric. In test_rotating_a_pseudonym_lands_the_buyer_in_a_crowd_not_on_themselves, `_assert_profile_carries_no_identity(plain, _T070_IDENTITY_VALUES)` scans the ENTIRE serialized profile — pseudonym included — for the literal '97205'. The pseudonyms here come from a live PseudonymVault, i.e. `psn-` + secrets.token_hex(16), and '97205' is all hex digits, so it appears by chance. The frozen T-070 test this graft copies from deliberately avoids the hazard by passing a FIXED pseudonym ('psn-7c1af204d9'), and the product documents and defends against exactly this class of false positive in `_distinguishable_from_entropy` ('A short all-hex identity fragment — the postal code 97205, say — turns up inside one by chance ... and treating that as a disclosure would fail real logins at random'). The graft, billed as 'a strict STRENGTHENING' of the frozen assertions, discards that protection.
findings.evidence: apps/buyer/svc/src/profile/__init__.py `_distinguishable_from_entropy` docstring names 97205 as the motivating case. apps/buyer/svc/src/vault/pseudonyms.py:50-69: PSEUDONYM_PREFIX='psn-', _ENTROPY_BYTES=16, default_pseudonym() = prefix + secrets.token_hex(16). 4,000,000-trial simulation: P('97205' in one 32-hex pseudonym) = 2.275e-05 (analytic 28*16^-5 = 2.67e-05); the test builds 3 vault pseudonyms, so ~6.8e-05 per run, about 1 spurious red per 14,600 runs.
findings.suggested_repair: Scan buckets only, not the whole profile, in the T-132 tests (`_assert_profile_carries_no_identity(plain['buckets'], ...)`), or mirror the product's rule — skip a fragment inside the pseudonym unless it is >= 8 characters or contains a non-hex character. The identity-KEY scan can stay on the whole profile; it is the VALUE scan over a random hex string that is unsound.

findings.problem: The positive control — the graft all three judges ranked first, and the one the amendment says stops 'the attack found nothing' and 'the attack is broken' being the same green — contains a conjunct that provably rejects nothing. `assert len(control) == len(population) and min(map(len, control.values())) == 1` over 30 accounts: if len(control) == 30 then 30 classes partition 30 buyers, so every class has exactly one member and min(...) == 1 is entailed. The second half of the guard can never fail when the first half passes. This is the project's signature failure mode reproduced inside the graft chosen to prevent it.
findings.evidence: Amendment edit 3, test_profile_buckets_are_k_anonymous_over_a_reference_population, the control assertion; `_reference_population()` returns 30 distinct accounts and `_equivalence_classes` appends one email per account, so sum of class sizes == 30 by construction.
findings.suggested_repair: Either drop the redundant conjunct and assert only `len(control) == len(population)`, or make the control meaningful by giving the population one deliberately duplicated pair (two buyers with byte-identical raw facets) and asserting `len(control) == len(population) - 1 and min(...) == 1 and max(...) == 2` — then both halves are falsifiable and the control also proves the classer merges identical vectors, not just that it separates different ones.

findings.problem: The 200-account cross-account sweep, sold in the summary as 'what rejects "truncate the free text to 24 chars"', rejects nothing the six hostile probes do not already reject. The sweep's only per-account assertion is the same `set(published) <= vocabulary` membership check that runs on hostile[0] ('hand-forged damascus chef knives ... batch 7734') roughly 200 builds earlier; a truncating implementation fails there first. Its closing non-growth assertion is textually the same assertion made six builds earlier. Two hundred build_profile calls are being spent to re-run a guard that has already fired. By the amendment's own stated bar — 'for every assertion you propose, state what input it REJECTS and what input it ADMITS' — I could not construct an implementation that passes the hostile probes and fails the sweep.
findings.evidence: Amendment edit 3: `_affinity` performs identical assertions for hostile probes and sweep accounts; the sweep inputs are `seed-%04d-widget-%x`, structurally the same shape as hostile[0] and hostile[4] which are probed first. Empirically every sabotage that failed the sweep also failed the hostile probes (self-interning vocab, truncation).
findings.suggested_repair: Make the sweep measure something the probes cannot: assert that the 200 unrelated accounts collapse into a small number of DISTINCT affinity lists (e.g. <= 4), which is a real anti-fingerprint property no single probe can express, and pair it with the coverage floor from finding 2 so the same loop also rejects the one-bit vocabulary. Otherwise cut it and say so.

findings.problem: The 'GREEN when earned' half of the Amendment 2 standard was never observed against any committed code. `apps/buyer/svc/src/profile/` does not exist on main — T-070 is unmerged — so the amendment's baseline of '7 failed, 2 passed' and its green run of '6 passed' were both measured in the f1-buyer worktree, with the fix supplied by a monkeypatching pytest plugin rather than by any file in the tree. On main the four new tests and the two frozen T-070 tests all fail with ModuleNotFoundError (9 failed, 0 passed for the E7 file), and history.csv cycle 7 records e7_buyer_passing = 0.0 against target 9.0. The amendment discloses the worktree and the prototype, so this is not concealment; but the proposal moves the e7_buyer_passing target 9 -> 13 on a branch where the measured value is 0 and the code the target describes is not present.
findings.evidence: `ls apps/buyer/svc/src/` on main: accept, auth, feedback, intent, main.py, vault — no profile/. Same path in proxyshop-worktrees/f1-buyer: profile/ present. .swarm-loop/history.csv:192 '7,e7_buyer_passing,0.0,9.0,...'.
